headline: Math is nearly solved; agents and real-world work remain the frontier
outlook: The past year closed 95% of the remaining headroom on math benchmarks, with FrontierMath reaching 90% in September, but only about a third of the headroom on agents and real work, where the Remote Labor Index sits at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%. That gap is narrowing from another direction: the length of tasks AI can handle has reached 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview and has been doubling roughly every four months, so on current trends a full 40-hour work-week is most likely around December, though the range runs to August 2027. At the same time, GPQA-level performance has fallen from $3.44 per million tokens with Gemini 2.5 Pro in March 2025 to $0.055 with Qwen3.7 Flash, and on a 24-fold yearly decline it would most likely drop below a cent in early 2027. Not everything follows the fitted curves, though: Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are both stuck below 90% months after their trends said they would cross it. Since past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, the safest reading is that the next year likely belongs to longer, cheaper agentic work, while the exact timing remains uncertain.
